The sentence says that when 2≠0 and 3≠0, “the quotient would be free of rank one.” But the preceding computation gives the cotangent fibre at the origin as Ω_A⊗_A k ≅ k². A free rank-one A-module has a one-dimensional fibre there, so the asserted freeness does not follow and is false. Removed the final freeness assertion; the fibre at the origin remains k².

The title says “Separable extensions have no differentials and inseparable ones do.” Without an algebraic or finite-extension restriction this is false: for k=Fp(t) and L=union_n Fp(t^(1/p^n)), L/k is purely inseparable, but every element of L has a pth root in L, so Ω_{L/k}=0. Narrowed the title to one finite separable case and one inseparable case; no universal inseparable claim remains.

The sentence calls α “the point” of Spec k in the fibre of Spec L→Spec k. Here α is an element of L, not a point of Spec k; Spec k has only its unique point, whose fibre is Spec L. Spec(L⊗_k L) is instead the fibre product obtained by pulling Spec L back along Spec L→Spec k. Replaced the false fibre-over-alpha sentence with the self-base-change Spec(L tensor_k L).

The statement concerns R⊗_Z S, while the witness computes L⊗_k L and uses a⊗1=1⊗a for a∈k. That equality is imposed in a tensor product over k, not over Z, so the displayed nilpotent witness does not establish the stated claim about R⊗_Z S. Narrowed the refuted claim to tensoring over k, exactly the base of the nilpotent witness; the direct page consumer remains accurate.

[F11] states that a module M has M_q=0 exactly when some g∉q annihilates M, with no finite-generation hypothesis. For R=Q[t], q=(0), and M=⊕_{a∈Q}R/(t−a), one has M_q=0, but no nonzero g∈R annihilates M: such a g would have to vanish at every rational a. Finite generation is needed for the claimed uniform annihilator. The proof uses the finitely generated ideal J, so a finite product of annihilators gives the required g outside q-prime.

The step calls D_j:K→K a “K′-linear derivation” extending ∂_j on K′. A K′-linear derivation must vanish on K′, whereas ∂_j(t_i)=δ_ij is nonzero for the relevant i. The construction can provide the needed k-derivation, but the stated linearity does not license the extension. Changed D_j to a k-derivation extending partial_j; the induced map Omega_{K/k}→K remains K-linear.

The step says that prescribing b↦0 on K[B0] defines a “K-derivation” extending D:K→L. A K-derivation vanishes on K, so it cannot extend a nonzero k-derivation D on K. The argument is repairable by constructing a k-derivation extending D and killing B0. Changed the polynomial-ring extension to a k-derivation, with D on K and zero on B0; compatibility is on K(B0).
